RestorePoint.Title: Create a system restore point?
RestorePoint.Description: Windows can take a snapshot of your system settings before anything changes. If something does not behave as expected, you can roll back to this point.
WhatChanges: Creates a restore point through Windows System Protection.
Does not change applications, files, or personal settings.
Benefits: Gives you a rollback point before tweaks and features are applied.
Takes only a few seconds and needs no restart.
RestorePoint.Info: Recommended on a fresh install. WinUtil still finishes the remaining steps if you choose No.

Install.Title: Choose applications to install
Install.Description: Pick the applications you want on this machine. WinUtil installs them with your preferred package manager and upgrades the ones that already have a newer version.
WhatChanges: Downloads and installs the selected applications.
Upgrades applications that already have a newer version available.
Benefits: One pass for all your apps.
Uses winget or Chocolatey according to your preference.
Install.Info: Nothing is installed until you press Apply all in order on the review screen.

Tweaks.Title: Apply a tweak preset?
Tweaks.Description: Presets are curated groups of Windows tweaks. Pick the level that matches how much you want to change.
WhatChanges: Standard: balanced defaults for most users.
Minimal: only the safest, least invasive tweaks.
Advanced: deeper changes for power users.
Benefits: No need to review every tweak individually.
You can undo the applied tweaks later from the Tweaks tab.
Tweaks.Info: Choosing None leaves your current tweaks untouched.
Tweaks.Warning: Advanced includes changes that may need a restart or sign-out.

Config.Title: Enable recommended Windows features?
Config.Description: Adds the .NET Framework versions that many older Windows applications still depend on.
WhatChanges: Enables .NET Framework 4 Advanced Services and .NET Framework 3.5.
May require a restart to finish.
Benefits: Older applications and installers run without missing-runtime errors.
Config.Info: Only a small, well-understood set of features is enabled here. Use the Advanced Config tab for anything else.

Updates.Title: Choose a Windows Update profile
Updates.Description: Windows Update can be left as it is, restored to defaults, set to recommended values, or disabled.
WhatChanges: Recommended: defers feature updates and configures download-and-notify.
Defaults: restores the Windows Update policies and services.
Disable: turns off Windows Update and its services.
Benefits: Applies a consistent update policy in one step.
Keep current makes no change at all.
Updates.Info: Disable Updates asks for confirmation before it runs.
Updates.Warning: Disabling Windows Update is not recommended: your machine stops receiving security fixes.

AppX.Title: Remove default AppX packages?
AppX.Description: Removes the pre-installed consumer apps that are usually not needed on a fresh Windows install.
WhatChanges: Removes the AppxDefault set of packaged apps for all users.
Stops those apps from being provisioned for new profiles.
Benefits: Less background activity from apps you do not use.
AppX.Info: You can restore most of these apps from the Microsoft Store later.
AppX.Warning: On a portable device this also removes built-in utilities you may rely on.

Review.Title: Review and apply
Review.Description: Check what you selected. Press Apply all in order to run the actions in the safest order.
WhatChanges: Restore point (if chosen), then tweaks, apps, features, AppX, and finally updates.
Benefits: One click runs everything in order.
Jobs are queued, so nothing runs at the same time.
Review.Info: Skipped steps are listed in the summary and are not applied.
